cold_open.hook: Meta's AI chatbot just got 20,000 Instagram accounts stolen—turns out the security feature was the vulnerability.

markets.macro_note: Chip strength masks Big Tech weakness; VIX crater signals complacency or relief.

big_story.story_title: Hackers likely hijacked over 20,000 Instagram accounts with Meta's AI chatbot
big_story.angle: Meta marketed its AI chatbot as a security feature—a way to catch phishing—and hackers weaponized it to steal accounts at scale. The irony isn't just embarrassing; it's a live case study in how AI safety theater becomes AI attack surface.

quick_hits.angle: Household financial anxiety hits highest level since July 2022—Fed rate cuts are priced in, but consumers aren't feeling it yet.
United CEO says there's 'nothing' to airline mergers after American rejected a deal—which is what every CEO says right before they do the thing.
Uber, Wayve, and Waymo are all racing robotaxis in London—the city that banned Uber once is now the proving ground for three different self-driving futures.
WhatsApp caught NSO spyware again, same group, after a court order—at some point 'caught' just means 'announced we found it again.'

odd_thing.joke_angle: Amazon's AI merch designer is just a print-on-demand machine that learned to hallucinate—finally, a tool for people who want their t-shirt to say something their brain couldn't.

yesterday_callback.topic: Anthropic IPO prices AI valuations at a moment when the market can't decide if AI is infrastructure or tulips.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Meta's chatbot getting weaponized to steal accounts is the market's answer: AI is neither infrastructure nor tulips—it's a liability with a venture-backed business model attached.

sign_off.callback_target: Meta's AI chatbot—the security feature that became the security breach.
